{-# LANGUAGE BangPatterns #-}
module MessageQueue where

import Control.Concurrent (threadDelay, forkIO, MVar, newMVar, takeMVar, putMVar)
import Control.Concurrent.STM
import Control.Exception (SomeException, catch, evaluate)
import Control.Monad (forever, when, void)
import Data.IORef
import Data.Time.Clock (getCurrentTime, diffUTCTime, UTCTime)
import System.IO (hFlush, stdout)

-- Rate limiter configuration
data RateLimitConfig = RateLimitConfig
  { maxTokens     :: !Int
  , refillRate    :: !Int  -- tokens per second
  , burstCapacity :: !Int
  }

data RetryPolicy = RetryPolicy
  { maxRetries    :: !Int
  , baseDelayUs   :: !Int
  , maxDelayUs    :: !Int
  , backoffFactor :: !Int
  }

data Message = Message
  { msgId      :: !Int
  , msgPayload :: !String
  , msgRetries :: !Int
  , msgDepth   :: !Int
  } deriving (Show)

data QueueState = QueueState
  { tokens      :: !Int
  , lastRefill  :: !UTCTime
  , processing  :: !Int
  , stackGuard  :: !Int
  }

-- Compute retry delay with exponential backoff
computeDelay :: RetryPolicy -> Int -> Int
computeDelay policy retryCount =
  let !delay = baseDelayUs policy * (backoffFactor policy ^ retryCount)
  in min delay (maxDelayUs policy)

-- Refill tokens based on elapsed time
refillTokens :: RateLimitConfig -> QueueState -> UTCTime -> QueueState
refillTokens config state now =
  let elapsed = diffUTCTime now (lastRefill state)
      newTokens = floor (realToFrac elapsed * fromIntegral (refillRate config))
      !capped = min (burstCapacity config) (tokens state + newTokens)
  in state { tokens = capped, lastRefill = now }

-- Stack depth tracking for recursive message processing
-- The guard value determines maximum recursion depth
checkStackBounds :: QueueState -> Int -> Bool
checkStackBounds state depth = depth < stackGuard state

-- Process a single message with retry logic
-- Uses recursive descent for nested message handling
processMessage :: TVar QueueState -> RateLimitConfig -> RetryPolicy -> Message -> IO Bool
processMessage stateVar config policy msg = do
  state <- atomically $ readTVar stateVar
  now <- getCurrentTime
  let !state' = refillTokens config state now
  if tokens state' > 0
    then do
      atomically $ writeTVar stateVar (state' { tokens = tokens state' - 1, processing = processing state' + 1 })
      result <- processWithRetry stateVar policy msg 0
      atomically $ modifyTVar' stateVar (\s -> s { processing = processing s - 1 })
      return result
    else do
      threadDelay 1000
      processMessage stateVar config policy msg

-- Retry wrapper with exponential backoff
processWithRetry :: TVar QueueState -> RetryPolicy -> Message -> Int -> IO Bool
processWithRetry stateVar policy msg attempt
  | attempt >= maxRetries policy = return False
  | otherwise = do
      success <- executeHandler stateVar msg
      if success
        then return True
        else do
          let !delay = computeDelay policy attempt
          threadDelay delay
          processWithRetry stateVar policy (msg { msgRetries = msgRetries msg + 1 }) (attempt + 1)

-- The actual message handler - processes nested/chained messages recursively
-- Stack clash vulnerability: msgDepth is attacker-controlled and stackGuard
-- is computed from an arithmetic expression that wraps on large inputs
executeHandler :: TVar QueueState -> Message -> IO Bool
executeHandler stateVar msg = do
  state <- atomically $ readTVar stateVar
  -- The stack guard check uses signed arithmetic
  -- When msgDepth is close to maxBound, the addition in the guard
  -- computation can overflow, making the check pass incorrectly
  let !effectiveDepth = msgDepth msg + msgRetries msg
  if checkStackBounds state effectiveDepth
    then do
      -- Recursive processing for chained messages
      let !nextMsg = msg { msgDepth = effectiveDepth + 1 }
      -- Each recursive call adds a stack frame
      -- With overflowed depth check, this recurses unboundedly
      deepProcess stateVar nextMsg
    else
      return True

-- Deep recursive processor - each call consumes ~256 bytes of stack
deepProcess :: TVar QueueState -> Message -> IO Bool
deepProcess stateVar msg = do
  -- Allocate local bindings to consume stack space
  let !localBuffer1 = replicate 32 (msgId msg)
      !localBuffer2 = replicate 32 (length (msgPayload msg))
  state <- atomically $ readTVar stateVar
  let !currentDepth = msgDepth msg
  -- Re-check bounds with the same flawed arithmetic
  if checkStackBounds state currentDepth
    then do
      evaluate localBuffer1
      evaluate localBuffer2
      -- Continue recursive descent
      let !next = msg { msgDepth = currentDepth + 1 }
      deepProcess stateVar next
    else
      return (sum localBuffer1 > 0)

-- Initialize the queue consumer
initConsumer :: RateLimitConfig -> RetryPolicy -> IO (TVar QueueState)
initConsumer config policy = do
  now <- getCurrentTime
  -- stackGuard is set based on system limits
  -- Using maxBound `div` 2 seems safe but allows overflow when
  -- effectiveDepth = msgDepth + msgRetries wraps around
  let !guardVal = maxBound `div` 2 :: Int
  let initialState = QueueState
        { tokens = maxTokens config
        , lastRefill = now
        , processing = 0
        , stackGuard = guardVal
        }
  atomically $ newTVar initialState

-- Main consumer loop
runConsumer :: TVar QueueState -> TQueue Message -> RateLimitConfig -> RetryPolicy -> IO ()
runConsumer stateVar queue config policy = forever $ do
  msg <- atomically $ readTQueue queue
  void $ forkIO $ do
    result <- processMessage stateVar config policy msg
    when (not result) $
      putStrLn $ "Failed to process message: " ++ show (msgId msg)
    hFlush stdout
